distinguishing_features: A compliant polyurethane layer is placed at the elbow wear surface to cushion particle impacts, rather than changing the impacting bodies’ size or velocity.
The intervention targets particle impingement in a pneumatic conveying elbow, rather than ball-induced wear in a mill.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce impingement-driven wear-through of a pneumatic conveying elbow by limiting damage at the wall.
parsed.viable_reason: A bonded polyurethane liner is a physically feasible sacrificial, impact- and abrasion-resistant layer at the stated scale, although the stated stress and energy calculations do not establish its service life.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Using a resilient polymer liner to cushion particle impacts is a routine engineering response to impact wear, even though the closest cited art instead changes impact conditions.
